20.0.0.en: A'nash: one who has six fingers on the foot or the hand.

20.0.1.en: This chapter was mentioned previously in (2 Sam 11:1, 12:26-31, 21:18-22). In it we find David's victory over the capital of the children of Ammon, the city of Rabbah, and his capture of it. Likewise his victory over the giants of the Philistines at Gezer and Gath.

20.0.2.en: People may boast of their strength, their wealth and their positions, or because of some capability they have, but all this is passing away. May you stand firm in your faith, knowing that the threats of the wicked are temporary and will come to an end, and that God allows them to test your faith and your humility.

20.0.4.en: 1- And Satan stood up against Israel, and provoked David to number Israel. 2- And David said to Joab and to the rulers of the people, Go, number Israel from Beersheba even to Dan; and bring the number of them to me, that I may know it. 3- And Joab answered, The Lord make his people an hundred times so many more as they be: but, my lord the king, are they not all my lord's servants? why then doth my lord require this thing? why will he be a cause of trespass to Israel? 4- Nevertheless the king's word prevailed against Joab. Wherefore Joab departed, and went throughout all Israel, and came to Jerusalem. 5- And Joab gave the sum of the number of the people unto David. And all they of Israel were a thousand thousand and an hundred thousand men that drew sword: and Judah was four hundred threescore and ten thousand men that drew sword. 6- But Levi and Benjamin counted he not among them: for the king's word was abominable to Joab. 7- And God was displeased with this thing; therefore he smote Israel. 8- And David said unto God, I have sinned greatly, because I have done this thing: but now, I beseech thee, do away the iniquity of thy servant; for I have done very foolishly. 9- And the Lord spake unto Gad, David's seer, saying, 10- Go and tell David, saying, Thus saith the Lord, I offer thee three things: choose thee one of them, that I may do it unto thee. 11- So Gad came to David, and said unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Choose thee 12- Either three years' famine; or three months to be destroyed before thy foes, while that the sword of thine enemies overtaketh thee; or else three days the sword of the Lord, even the pestilence, in the land, and the angel of the Lord destroying throughout all the coasts of Israel. Now therefore advise thyself what word I shall bring again to him that sent me. 13- And David said unto Gad, I am in a great strait: let me fall now into the hand of the Lord; for very great are his mercies: but let me not fall into the hand of man. 14- So the Lord sent pestilence upon Israel: and there fell of Israel seventy thousand men. 15- And God sent an angel unto Jerusalem to destroy it: and as he was destroying, the Lord beheld, and he repented him of the evil, and said to the angel that destroyed, It is enough, stay now thine hand. And the angel of the Lord stood by the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite. 16- And David lifted up his eyes, and saw the angel of the Lord stand between the earth and the heaven, having a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem. Then David and the elders of Israel, who were clothed in sackcloth, fell upon their faces. 17- And David said unto God, Is it not I that commanded the people to be numbered? even I it is that have sinned and done evil indeed; but as for these sheep, what have they done? let thine hand, I pray thee, O Lord my God, be on me, and on my father's house; but not on thy people, that they should be plagued. 18- Then the angel of the Lord commanded Gad to say to David, that David should go up, and set up an altar unto the Lord in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite. 19- And David went up at the saying of Gad, which he spake in the name of the Lord. 20- And Ornan turned back, and saw the angel; and his four sons with him hid themselves. Now Ornan was threshing wheat. 21- And as David came to Ornan, Ornan looked and saw David, and went out of the threshingfloor, and bowed himself to David with his face to the ground. 22- Then David said to Ornan, Grant me the place of this threshingfloor, that I may build an altar therein unto the Lord: thou shalt grant it me for the full price: that the plague may be stayed from the people.

20.0.5.en: 23- And Ornan said unto David, Take it to thee, and let my lord the king do that which is good in his eyes: lo, I give thee the oxen also for burnt offerings, and the threshing instruments for wood, and the wheat for the meat offering; I give it all. 24- And king David said to Ornan, Nay; but I will verily buy it for the full price: for I will not take that which is thine for the Lord, nor offer burnt offerings without cost. 25- So David gave to Ornan for the place six hundred shekels of gold by weight. 26- And David built there an altar unto the Lord, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and called upon the Lord; and he answered him from heaven by fire upon the altar of burnt offering. 27- And the Lord commanded the angel; and he put up his sword again into the sheath thereof. 28- At that time when David saw that the Lord had answered him in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite, then he sacrificed there.

20.0.6.en: 29- For the tabernacle of the Lord, which Moses made in the wilderness, and the altar of the burnt offering, were at that season in the high place at Gibeon. 30- But David could not go before it to enquire of God: for he was afraid because of the sword of the angel of the Lord.

22.0.0.en: After David saw with his own eyes the fire come down from heaven and accept his burnt offerings and sacrifices, he felt that this was the place God had chosen for the building of His Temple, so he set about with all diligence and joy to prepare the building materials for this Temple, to help his son Solomon, because he was young in age and the Temple would be great, to befit the greatness of God. It may seem strange that God chose the threshing floor of a Gentile man, Ornan the Jebusite, on which to build His Temple, but God declares here in the Old Testament that He will die to redeem the Jews and the Gentiles, and that His Church will be of all the peoples who believe in Him.

22.0.1.en: The place where the Temple was built was a threshing floor, that is, a place for gathering wheat and separating the grain from the chaff, and this is what will happen in the Church of the New Testament, of which John the Baptist spoke clearly in his Gospel (Mt 3:12).

22.1.0.en: The strangers: the Canaanites who live among the children of Israel.

22.1.1.en: David employed the pagan Canaanites in the heavy labor, which was hewing the stones with which the Temple would be built, and he put them to this work. The participation of the Gentiles in the building of the Temple is a type of their acceptance into the Church of the New Testament with the Jews.

22.1.2.en: Solomon also employed these strangers in the work of building the Temple, and their number is mentioned, which is 153,600 (2 Chr 2:17). Thus we see the sharing of David and Solomon in the building of the Temple, and both are types of Christ: David is a type of Christ's humility and endurance, and Solomon is a type of Christ's power and authority.

22.2.0.en: Doors: the leaves of the doors.

22.2.1.en: Joinings: the metal parts that join the doors to their jambs, which are called hinges. David also prepared large quantities of iron and brass; gifts had come to him from the surrounding nations, in addition to the spoil he took from the lands he conquered. Although brass was scarce in those times, David prepared a very great amount of it, which he could not count because of its abundance.

22.3.0.en: The Zidonians: the inhabitants of Zidon, a coastal city lying on the Mediterranean Sea north of the land of the Jews (present-day Lebanon), famous for fishing and for skill in cutting timber. The Tyrians: the inhabitants of Tyre, a coastal city lying on the Mediterranean Sea, north of the land of the Jews (present-day Lebanon) and south of Zidon; it was one of the greatest commercial cities in the world, and was famous for skill in cutting timber.

22.3.1.en: David also prepared large quantities of precious cedar wood, which reached him from the Tyrians and the Zidonians.

22.4.0.en: Tender: the small plant before it ripens, and what is meant here is that he is young, his character and strength not yet complete.

22.4.1.en: David's concern in preparing for the house of God had two reasons behind it:

22.4.2.en: 1- His love for God, which made him concerned to prepare for His house, and he was not troubled, because of his humility, that God had forbidden him to build the house.

22.4.3.en: 2- His love for his son Solomon, who felt the difficulty of the responsibility upon him because of his young age, for he began his reign when he was twenty years old.

22.4.4.en: May you be concerned to help those around you, especially in spiritual works and service, even if your name does not appear in this work. Be humble, and it is enough blessing for you that you shared in the service of God.

22.5.0.en: The most important thing David charged his son with was the building of the house of God, and he called God the God of Israel, because they were the only people at that time who worshiped God in the midst of the pagan nations, and therefore they are responsible for magnifying His name and worshiping Him, that perhaps the nations may understand and believe in Him.

22.6.0.en: David made clear to Solomon his desire to build the house of God, and that he had told God of this desire of his.

22.7.0.en: God refused David's desire to build a house for Him, because of his involvement in many wars with the surrounding nations, during which he killed many of them, or perhaps because of his killing of Uriah the husband of Bathsheba. God wanted the one who builds His house to be marked by calm and peace, because His house is a place of rest and peace for hearts. God promised David that He would give him a son whom he would name Solomon, whose days would be characterized by calm, as the peoples would be subject to him, so that he would be free for this great work, which was the building of the house of God.

22.8.0.en: God also promised to care for Solomon, so that he would be called a son to God and his kingdom would be established forever, because from his descendants Christ would come, who reigns forever.

22.8.1.en: Solomon here is a type of Christ, the only Son of the Father, who reigns forever. And thus we see that God worked through David to subdue the peoples who opposed His people. He also works through Solomon to build His house, for God is the worker in both, so that no one may be proud, just as He worked through Moses to bring the people out of Egypt, cross the wilderness, receive the commandments and build the tabernacle of meeting, while the possession of the land of Canaan was by the hand of Joshua.

22.9.1.en: After David had told his son Solomon the commands of God, he encouraged him to prepare for the building of the Temple, confident that God would make him succeed. Here we remember God's encouragement to Joshua, that he should arise and possess the land of Canaan (Josh 1:7, 8).

22.10.1.en: Judgments: the commandments and the Law.

22.10.3.en: David charged Solomon to hold fast to the Law of God and His worship, for this is the foundation by which God is pleased, so that He will be with him, and then he will be able to build a temple for God, and God will give him wisdom and understanding to construct this great house. Solomon's responsibility is not only to hold fast to the statutes and judgments, but to lead his people to hold fast to them, and then he will be a king from God, to accomplish His purposes.

22.10.4.en: In the end David encouraged Solomon to carry out his responsibilities and not to fear any problems that might stand in his way, because God is his supporter and the One who works in him.

22.11.0.en: To encourage Solomon, David told him about the period of his reign, in which he suffered the troubles of the surrounding nations and problems within his kingdom, such as the rising up of his son Absalom against him. During this suffering, David's heart was occupied with the building of the house of God, so he prepared:

22.11.1.en: 1- The building materials, in abundance beyond human expectations, which are:

22.11.3.en: b- A million talents of silver

22.11.4.en: c- Brass and iron without number

22.11.5.en: d- Timber and stone without number

22.11.6.en: 2- He also prepared craftsmen skilled in all the fields that the Temple needs, such as stonecutters, builders, carpenters ....

22.11.7.en: In the end David called Solomon to arise and build the house of God.

22.11.8.en: To succeed in any work, you must rely on God by obeying His commandments and holding fast to His worship, that is, your prayers, your fasts and all that you learn from the Church, in addition to constant repentance, that you may remain pure and a vessel fit for the work of God.

22.12.s.en: (3) David's charge to the leaders of the people

22.12.0.en: David gathered the leaders of the people and reminded them how God had given them rest and peace, by subduing to them all the surrounding peoples by the hand of David.

22.13.0.en: David charged the leaders to be concerned to love God with all their hearts, for it is the most important thing in life, and then they would be able to come forward to build His Temple, and place in it the ark of His covenant and the holy vessels. By this David supported his son Solomon, as he made the leaders of the people supporters of him in building this great Temple.

22.13.1.en: To be able to succeed in any work, your heart must be with God, and as you love Him you trust in Him, and go forward with confidence and strength and succeed in everything your hands reach for, and do not fear any troubles that may meet you. The service of the Levites. Chapters 23-26 speak of the service of the Levites for the Temple of God, and each chapter speaks of one of their classes, and this chapter speaks of the service of the Levites in general.

23.0.0.en: Solomon was not David's firstborn, but God chose him by name to be David's successor on his throne. So when David was old, that is, at the end of his sixties (for he died at the age of seventy), he made Solomon king in Jerusalem, so that his brothers would not oppose him, as Adonijah tried to seize the kingship.

23.1.0.en: David gathered the leaders of the people and also all the priests and the Levites, and by this he established Solomon's kingship, and he involved the leaders in the preparation for the service of the Temple. Then he commanded that the Levites be numbered from thirty years old and upward, and their number was 38,000, which is about four times their number in the days of Moses, when it was 8,580 (Num 4:47, 48). Here we see David's concern for arranging the service of the Temple and not only its building, for the service that is carried out in it is more important than its building, and all this shows David's great love for God, who until the end of his life, despite his old age, was concerned for the service of God.

23.1.1.en: Because David's numbering of the Levites was on account of preparing them for the service of the Temple, God did not punish him, as He punished him when he numbered the men of war, for the aim was the love of God and not pride.

23.1.2.en: If the love of God reigns over your heart, you will be concerned for His service, and indeed you will continue in this throughout your life, because through it you touch God and enjoy His blessings.

23.2.1.en: David divided the Levites into groups as follows:

23.2.2.en: 1- He appointed 24 divisions, each of 1000 men, to help in the service of the Temple. Each division served for a week, that is, each division served twice every year.

23.2.3.en: 2- He also appointed six thousand of the Levites as officers and judges, to decide disputes among the people.

23.2.4.en: 3- He also assigned four thousand to guard the Temple, or as doorkeepers; the details of their service are mentioned in (ch. 9, ch. 26).

23.2.5.en: 4- And he appointed another four thousand to praise with musical instruments.

23.2.7.en: The legal age for service is thirty years, but sometimes Levites of 25 or 20 years and above were added to the service, according to need, and they would help the Levites who were thirty years old and above (Num 4:3, Num 8:24).
